subject.title: Bound HTTP error body snippets to readable streams

question: Should non-readable Response adapters intentionally lose their diagnostic body text so the shared helper can guarantee bounded memory use?
rationale: No standard bounded or cancellable prefix operation exists when an adapter exposes only whole-body text() or arrayBuffer(), so retaining diagnostics and guaranteeing the byte cap require an explicit contract choice.

options.title: Accept the fail-closed fallback
options.body: Return an empty snippet without a readable stream, preserve status and headers, and merge after required checks pass.

options.title: Define a bounded adapter contract
options.body: Pause the PR and add an explicit bounded-prefix interface for non-standard adapters that must preserve diagnostic text.

options.title: Retain shipped diagnostics
options.body: Decline this change and continue accepting whole-body buffering for adapters without readable streams.

recommendation.title: Accept the fail-closed fallback
recommendation.body: Return an empty snippet without a readable stream, preserve status and headers, and merge after required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion identifies their recent external-provider response-bounding work as the closest ownership signal for this compatibility choice.
